title: Youth interest in clean-energy work is high, but the pathway from learning to paid participation remains fragmented
source_unit: UNDP / Goodwall, Powering the future: Sparking the next generation of energy talent, September 2026, with partner publication context from Goodwall and UNDP contributors
geography: Global youth and sustainable-energy workforce pathways, with engagement spanning more than 100 countries

denominator.unit: young people reached across more than 100 countries through a free mobile-first sustainable-energy learning and engagement program, approximate

reach.value: more than 58,000 young people were reached; 55,314 completed the learning journey

geographic_scope.value: engagement spanned more than 100 countries, with examples including Kenya, the Philippines, India, Costa Rica, Haiti, and Papua New Guinea

participation_route.value: the program combined sustainable-energy learning, a knowledge check, and an invitation to connect the topic to participants' communities

analytic_signal.value: energy-transition workforce formation is being treated as a participation and opportunity problem, not only a technology or investment problem

observations.method: UNDP and Goodwall learning and engagement program with public reporting on reach and completion; this is a program frame, not a probability sample.
observations.uncertainty: Reach and completion counts describe program participation and cannot be generalized to all young people or interpreted as representative labor-market demand.
observations.subgroup: Young people engaging with a mobile-first sustainable-energy learning program across multiple countries.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large digital reach may reflect platform distribution and motivated participation rather than a broad shift in youth attitudes or workforce supply.

denominator.unit: post-program participant survey reported in the UNDP/Goodwall energy-talent publication

career_interest.unit: percent of post-program survey respondents expressing interest in a clean-energy career

concrete_next_step.unit: percent choosing at least one concrete next step

opportunity_gap.value: interest and stated next steps were stronger than participants' visibility into training, practical experience, mentors, credentials, and entry-level opportunities

analytic_signal.value: the emerging demand signal is not simply awareness of green energy; it is a desire for a legible route from learning to earning

observations.method: Post-program survey associated with the UNDP/Goodwall initiative; the publication does not establish a representative youth sample or a causal effect of the course.
observations.uncertainty: The survey denominator, recruitment process, question wording, nonresponse, and pre-program baseline limit population inference and before-after causal interpretation.
observations.subgroup: Post-program participants who completed or responded to the program survey.
observations.counterinterpretation: Participants may have entered with unusually high interest in sustainability, so the percentages may overstate interest in the wider youth population.

denominator.unit: participants completing the reported program quiz

role_breadth.unit: percent answering that most clean-energy jobs are not engineering roles, as reported

job-growth_knowledge.unit: percent correctly answering a question about projected clean-energy job creation by 2050, as reported

pathway_constraint.value: career and employment knowledge were among the weakest measured areas

analytic_signal.value: the skills bottleneck includes occupational information and career navigation, not only technical training capacity

observations.method: Program quiz results reported in a public UNDP/Goodwall partner account; quiz completion is not an independent measure of labor-market skill or employment readiness.
observations.uncertainty: The item wording, scoring, country mix, prior knowledge, and relation between quiz performance and later employment are not sufficient for causal or population claims.
observations.subgroup: 5,078 participants who completed the program quiz.
observations.counterinterpretation: A short course quiz may capture unfamiliarity with terminology rather than a durable lack of occupational knowledge or capability.

observations.period: 2026; proposed response to the youth energy-talent gap

proposed_connectors.value: the partners describe or propose an energy-innovation incubator, links between online learning and offline experience, national energy dialogues, continued learning, work-based learning, and support for youth-led enterprises

institutional_roles.value: governments, employers, education providers, finance, and energy institutions each have a role in making the pathway visible and usable

implementation_boundary.value: the proposed connectors are not evidence of completed placements, employment, earnings, retention, or influence on energy decisions

open_test.value: join course completion to credential recognition, apprenticeship or placement access, first job, retention, earnings, entrepreneurship, and meaningful participation in energy planning

observations.method: Public policy and program synthesis based on the UNDP/Goodwall energy-talent publication and partner commentary.
observations.uncertainty: The publication sets out a pathway agenda but does not report a longitudinal employment evaluation or implementation results for the proposed connectors.
observations.subgroup: Young people, energy employers, training institutions, public energy agencies, finance providers, and youth-led enterprises.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal pathways may not be necessary for every participant; informal networks, local enterprise, or self-directed learning may produce opportunity outside the proposed program architecture.

related_sources.claim: Goodwall and UNDP contributors publicly describe the program reach, interest, quiz, and pathway findings that contextualize the UNDP publication.
UNDP's energy hub supplies the broader energy-access, transition, finance, youth, and inclusive-development context.

boundary: This record adds a youth-to-workforce pathway from clean-energy interest and program learning through occupational information, practical experience, credentials, employment, entrepreneurship, and energy-governance participation. It uses aggregate program and published survey/quiz reporting, not respondent-level data, a representative youth survey, a labor-market forecast, or proof that the proposed pathways produced jobs or policy influence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The UNDP publications and energy pages were reviewed for the publication title, program framing, and energy-transition context; the public Goodwall/UNDP contributor account was reviewed for reach, completion, survey, quiz, and proposed-pathway figures.
